methodological_rigor.justification: Rigorous preclinical study combining scRNA-seq analysis (human GBM, GSE160189; murine CT2A, GSE236243), flow cytometry across multiple tumor models (CT2A, E0771, Yummer1.7 in subcutaneous and intracranial settings), bulk RNA-seq of sorted TIM3+ cells (n=6 WT, n=6 KO), adoptive transfer experiments with competitive co-transfer design, and in vivo pharmacologic TNFR2 antagonism with anti-PD-1 (n=20 per group). The use of multiple independent tumor models and chronic LCMV infection to validate findings is a methodological strength. Statistical methods include appropriate paired/unpaired t-tests, two-way ANOVA, and log-rank tests with Bonferroni correction for multiple comparisons. Confounders are addressed through competitive adoptive transfer and CD8-depletion experiments establishing T-cell specificity.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: The study identifies TNFR2 as a potential upstream regulator of TOX-mediated T-cell exhaustion and demonstrates that TNFR2 antagonism synergizes with anti-PD-1 to achieve 50–60% long-term survival in intracranial GBM models — a notably immunotherapy-resistant tumor. These findings have clear translational implications for TNFR2 as a therapeutic target in combination with checkpoint blockade. However, all mechanistic and therapeutic experiments are in murine systems; human validation is limited to scRNA-seq re-analysis showing TNFR2 expression on TILs in GBM specimens. LoE is 5 (basic science/preclinical).

reporting_quality.justification: The paper follows ARRIVE-adjacent reporting with IACUC approval documented, animal numbers per group specified, cell line authentication (Mycoplasma-negative), and randomization by age/gender. Statistical methods are fully specified with multiple comparison corrections and sample sizes per group. Raw RNA-seq data are deposited in GEO (GSE297330) and custom R scripts are provided (redacted in blinded version). Antibody details with RRID numbers are provided in Table 1. Some minor gaps remain in describing batch effects for RNA-seq and complete reporting of all supplementary figure group sizes.

novelty_literature.justification: While TNFR2 has been studied in Treg biology and as a potential cancer target, its role as an upstream regulator of TOX expression in exhausted CD8+ T cells is novel. The discovery of a PD-1+TIM3+TOXlo T-cell population that uncouples TIM3 and TOX expression challenges the established exhaustion hierarchy and represents a mechanistically original finding. The synergistic combination of TNFR2 antagonism with anti-PD-1 achieving durable responses in an intracranial GBM model — one of the most immunotherapy-resistant tumors — is a significant translational advance. This work fills a documented gap in understanding upstream regulators of the TOX exhaustion program.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is clearly written with a logical progression from scRNA-seq correlation analyses to genetic knockout to pharmacologic validation. The narrative coherently builds the case for TNFR2 as an upstream TOX regulator. Figures are well-designed and comprehensive with appropriate statistical annotations. The discussion thoughtfully contextualizes the novel TIM3+TOXlo population and its implications. Minor issues include some redundancy between figure legends and results text, and the discussion of TNFR2 on non-T cells is appropriately flagged as a limitation.

key_strengths: Novel mechanistic discovery positioning TNFR2 as an upstream regulator of TOX-mediated T-cell exhaustion, supported by multi-model genetic and pharmacologic validation
Discovery of a novel PD-1+TIM3+TOXlo T-cell population that challenges established exhaustion hierarchy — a conceptually important finding for the field
Pharmacologic TNFR2 antagonism + anti-PD-1 synergy achieving 50–60% long-term survival in immunotherapy-resistant intracranial GBM models with durable memory rechallenge protection
Rigorous methodological design with competitive adoptive transfer, CD8-depletion controls, and RNA-seq data deposited in GEO with available analysis scripts
key_concerns: Human validation limited to scRNA-seq re-analysis of a single public GBM dataset; no functional validation of TNFR2 pathway in human T cells
Therapeutic benefit observed only with TRP2-engineered tumors containing a rejection antigen in most in vivo models; the parental CT2A data are shown but less prominently characterized
Mechanism by which TNFR2 signals upstream of NFAT/TOX is not fully elucidated; exact signaling pathway between TNFR2 and the NFAT-TOX axis remains correlative
chief_reviewer.rationale: This mechanistically rigorous preclinical study identifies TNFR2 as a novel upstream regulator of T-cell exhaustion with compelling multi-model genetic and pharmacologic validation; the discovery of the TIM3+TOXlo population and anti-PD-1 synergy in GBM are field-advancing findings that merit Tier 1 consideration, pending human functional validation.
